author: potuz
content:
We don't need things in the spec before going to devnet, on the other direction we do need to implement the spec on our trunk branches to pass test vectors or skip possibly important tests (all tests that failed when the feature was added). This forces clients to implement in their trunk branches everything that goes on the specs repo regardless if it's SFId or not, which ultimately leads to whatever is on the spec to decide the scope of the fork instead of ACD. Once a feature lands in the repo the onus is on removing it rather than on sfiing it. 

If you need the features merged in the spec for devnet testing I'd say we do what we always did before which was the main branch plus feature branches that were being tested

author: potuz
content:
I think I wasn't clear what "failed test" means here. 

The fork is Heze, we have some tests. Code in our main branch passes it. 

A feature is added. That feature adds it's own tests. Skipping those tests is fine.

However, when a feature is added, existing tests also fail without fixing them to account for the new behavior. If we skip those tests then we stop testing the original code we meant to test. Skipping these tests is not fine
